old: This corrects the corpus's own record, which said Buildkite supplies 'the scheduler and the agent binary' and that 'the machine the agent runs on is the customer's, or a Buildkite-hosted agent on a paid plan', and which recorded no shape. That was wrong on 2026-10-24: Buildkite's own limits table gives the Free plan 2,000 Linux vCPU-minutes of hosted agents and 20 vCPU of concurrency, and its Linux hosted-agent page restricts the Free plan to the small 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 47 GB shape. So Buildkite does sell a free machine, it is 2 vCPU and 4 GB, and it needs no card. The corpus also had the arithmetic backwards: it priced the pool against a 4 vCPU agent, but a Free-plan namespace cannot select one. At 2 vCPU the pool is 16 h 40 min a month, not 8 h 20 min. Not established: the egress term; whether a hosted agent can be reached inbound (no page read says it can, and the environment is destroyed at job end); and whether the 2,000 vCPU-minutes includes the boot time of the agent, which the limits page says consumes concurrency 'from the time it starts booting' but does not say whether it consumes minutes.
new: Boot time does not draw on the pool: usage is billed on job runtime and excludes startup and shutdown. Not established: the egress term, and whether a hosted agent can be reached inbound (no page read says it can, and the environment is destroyed at job end).
